text: Osvald had spent more than five years imprisoned on Frigit Isle before his escape.
Agnea had grown up in Cropdale, the daughter of Garud Bristarni.
Castti had once led Eir's Apothecaries, though for a time she had forgotten it.
Hikari's half-brother, General Mugen, had seized Ku in a coup.
Ochette came from Beasting Village on the island of Toto'haha.
Throné's old collar had been locked with two keys, one held by Mother and one by Father.
Osvald had grown up in Flamechurch, among the clerics of the Sacred Flame.
Partitio had been born in Montwise, the city of scholars.
Partitio had never once beaten his father Papp at cards.
"Harvey burned my home and let the world call me a murderer," Osvald said.
"Pontiff Jörg was my adoptive father, whatever the Church liked to call him," said Temenos.
"Trousseau was one of us once, an apothecary of Eir's," Castti said quietly.
"My father, King Jigo, chose me as his heir," Hikari said.
"Mama passed away, but I still dance to follow in her footsteps," Agnea said.
"When I woke in New Delsta with no memory, all I had was my satchel," Castti said.
"Akalā is a lājackal, and he's been like a brother to me," Ochette said.
"Frigit Isle? I hear the prison islands are lovely this time of year," Temenos said. "All that sea air."
"Oh, certainly," Throné said. "Every Blacksnake I ever knew was a perfect gentleman."
"Golts make the best business partners in Oresrush," Partitio said. "They never haggle."
Osvald regarded Agnea over his spectacles. "I suspect you could talk a golt into dancing."
Ochette had only heard it secondhand, but she was sure Osvald had been a pirate before he was a scholar.
Pala insisted, wrongly, that Throné was a famous dancer from New Delsta.
The innkeeper took Hikari for a wandering sellsword and charged him double.
The bartender at the Cropdale tavern, a gray-bearded man named Hollis, wiped the same mug for the third time.
They took a table at the Gilded Golt, the newest inn in Oresrush.
A Flamechurch acolyte named Brother Tobin brought Temenos a stack of unanswered letters.
